The 21-year-old is often compared to Argentina's legendary Diego Maradona. Fernando Torres (Liverpool, Spain) The Spaniard enjoyed an incredible first season in the Premier League -- scoring 24 league goals for Liverpool -- a new record for a foreign striker in his debut season. After that success he went on to Austria-Switzerland and played an integral part in Spain's Euro 2008 victory, scoring the winning goal in the final. If top-level international performances are the key to this award then Torres should go close. Iker Casillas (Real Madrid, Spain) Casillas was recently awarded the Best Keeper of the World in 2008 title by the International Federation of Football History and Statistics. Casillas played a large part in helping his Real Madrid side to the Spanish La Liga title, put in strong performances in the UEFA Champions League, and was a key part of Spain's Euro 2008-winning team. Xavi Hernandez (Barcelona, Spain) Also part of the Spanish team which won Euro 2008, Xavi claimed the Player of the Tournament award, which would make him a worthy winner of the FIFA Player of the Year. Aside from his stunning performances at Euro, Xavi scored seven goals for Barcelona last season, and was one of their standout players, while this season he has continued his good form and helped Barcelona to the top of La Liga.

# Ronaldo leads star-studded race for FIFA world honor

**ZURICH, Switzerland (CNN) —** Cristiano Ronaldo will be the overwhelming favorite when FIFA names its 2008 World Player of the Year, but the Manchester United winger faces competition from Lionel Messi, Fernando Torres, Xavi and reigning winner Kaká.

The award, decided by the coaches and captains of national teams, will be presented at FIFA’s gala in Zurich on January 12, 2009.

## Cristiano Ronaldo: The man to beat

Ronaldo enters the ceremony after a remarkable year in which he inspired Manchester United to both the English Premier League title and the Champions League trophy.

The Portugal international scored 42 goals in all competitions during the 2007-08 season, including eight in Europe. He also found the net in the Champions League final against Chelsea before United prevailed on penalties in Moscow.

Already crowned the 2008 Ballon d’Or winner, Ronaldo appears well placed to complete a sweep of football’s leading individual prizes.

## Lionel Messi: The closest challenger

Barcelona’s Messi did not collect the same club honors as Ronaldo in 2008, but his individual performances strengthened his reputation as one of the game’s most gifted players.

The Argentine combined close control, acceleration and creativity to devastating effect and helped his country win Olympic gold in Beijing. His increasingly influential role at Barcelona has made him Ronaldo’s most serious long-term rival for football’s top individual awards.

## Fernando Torres: A dream year

Torres enjoyed a spectacular first season in England, scoring 33 goals for Liverpool and quickly establishing himself as one of Europe’s most dangerous strikers.

His defining moment came on the international stage. Torres scored the only goal as Spain defeated Germany in the Euro 2008 final, ending his country’s 44-year wait for a major trophy.

That combination of club goals and international success gives the 24-year-old a strong case.

## Xavi: Spain’s midfield architect

While Torres delivered the decisive goal in Vienna, Xavi was the player who set Spain’s rhythm throughout the European Championship.

The Barcelona midfielder was named UEFA’s player of the tournament after directing Spain’s possession-based attack with his passing, movement and composure. His candidacy reflects not only personal excellence but also the growing recognition of the creative midfielder’s role in Spain’s historic triumph.

## Kaká: The reigning champion

Brazilian playmaker Kaká returns as the holder of the award after winning in 2007, when he led AC Milan to Champions League glory.

His 2008 campaign was less dominant, with Milan missing out on Europe’s premier club competition, but Kaká’s vision, technique and goalscoring ability ensured he remained among the game’s elite performers.

## Verdict

Messi’s brilliance, Torres’ goals and Xavi’s influence make this one of the strongest shortlists in recent years. Yet Ronaldo’s combination of statistics, trophies and match-winning performances sets him apart.

After conquering England and Europe with Manchester United, the Portuguese star is expected to end his extraordinary year on top of the world.

# FIFA Player of the Year 2008: Leading Contenders

Cristiano Ronaldo entered the race for the 2008 FIFA World Player of the Year award as the clear favorite. His extraordinary scoring record and central role in Manchester United’s Premier League and UEFA Champions League triumphs gave him the strongest claim, although Lionel Messi and Spain’s European champions provided serious competition.

## Cristiano Ronaldo — The Favorite

Ronaldo enjoyed a spectacular 2007–08 season with Manchester United, scoring 42 goals in all competitions. The Portuguese winger combined pace, skill and aerial ability with increasingly ruthless finishing. He helped United secure the Premier League title and scored in the Champions League final against Chelsea. Having already won the 2008 Ballon d’Or, Ronaldo was widely expected to take FIFA’s top individual honor as well.

## Lionel Messi

Messi was already emerging as Ronaldo’s principal long-term rival. The Barcelona forward’s close control, acceleration and creativity made him one of football’s most dangerous attacking players. Injuries limited parts of his club season, but he remained outstanding when available and helped Argentina win the gold medal at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

## Fernando Torres

Torres made an immediate impact after joining Liverpool from Atlético Madrid. The Spanish striker scored 33 goals in his debut season in England, setting a new standard for a foreign newcomer in the Premier League era. His speed and composed finishing also proved decisive for Spain, most notably when he scored the winning goal against Germany in the Euro 2008 final.

## Iker Casillas

Casillas strengthened his reputation as one of the world’s finest goalkeepers during 2008. He captained Real Madrid to the Spanish league title and then led Spain to victory at Euro 2008. His saves in the quarter-final penalty shootout against Italy were particularly important, helping Spain overcome a major psychological barrier on the way to the trophy.

## Xavi

Xavi was the creative heartbeat of Spain’s triumphant Euro 2008 team and was named the tournament’s best player by UEFA. Operating in central midfield, he dictated tempo through intelligent movement, precise passing and exceptional awareness. Although Barcelona endured an inconsistent club campaign, Xavi’s influence during Spain’s first major international triumph in 44 years made him a compelling candidate.

## Verdict

Messi’s brilliance, Torres’s goals, Casillas’s leadership and Xavi’s midfield control all defined 2008. Nevertheless, Ronaldo’s combination of individual statistics and major club trophies made him the outstanding favorite—and he ultimately won the 2008 FIFA World Player of the Year award.
